articles.title: 'Nashe ka highway': Cops found lying intoxicated, service INSAS rifle left unattended; both suspended
articles.summary: RAIPUR: An assistant sub-inspector and a constable posted in Durg district were suspended after they were found allegedly intoxicated and tipsy near the
articles.body: RAIPUR: An assistant sub-inspector and a constable posted in Durg district were suspended after they were found allegedly intoxicated and tipsy near the bus stand in Ambikapur on Monday morning, with the ASI's service INSAS rifle lying unattended nearby.The two personnel - ASI Prakash Ekka and constable Rishikant Tripathi - had been sent from Durg on Oct 17 in connection with escorting a prisoner to Ambikapur central jail.Police said the prisoner was lodged in the jail on Oct 18, after which the two personnel reached the bus stand to return to Durg.On Monday morning, local residents found both policemen lying near a roadside kiosk in an apparently intoxicated condition. The ASI's INSAS rifle was also found unattended close to them. Videos of the incident were recorded by bystanders and later circulated on social media.Rifle secured, Durg SP orders suspensionResidents informed the bus stand police outpost, following which a police team reached the spot and took the rifle into safe custody.Surguja SP Rajesh Agrawal informed Durg SP Vijay Agrawal about the incident. The Durg SP subsequently suspended both personnel and attached them to the police lines pending further departmental action.The incident has raised serious questions over weapon security and conduct while on escort duty, particularly as the personnel were carrying a service firearm during official deployment.Further departmental inquiry is expected to examine how the weapon was left unattended and whether the personnel had consumed alcohol while still on duty.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Raipur | Silver Rate in Raipur | Bank Holidays in Raipur | Public Holidays in Raipur | Raipur AQI | Weather in Raipur | Petrol Price in Raipur | Diesel Price in Raipur | CNG Price in Raipur | LPG Price in RaipurStay updated with the latest Raipur news. articles.title: 9 heads, 300 years of worship: Ravana gets police protection in this MP town, not a pyre
articles.summary: BHOPAL: While police across the country oversee Dussehra celebrations that culminate in Ravana's effigy going up in flames, a police station in Madhya
articles.body: BHOPAL: While police across the country oversee Dussehra celebrations that culminate in Ravana's effigy going up in flames, a police station in Madhya Pradesh's Satna district does something rather unusual, it protects the demon king who's worshipped here by devotees.Inside the premises of Kothi police station stands a 25-foot-tall, 22-foot-wide Ravana idol, believed to be at least 300 years old, where generations of a priest's family have performed rituals on Dussehra.Unlike the familiar 10-headed depiction, this Ravana has nine heads. Local belief has it that he offered one of his heads to Lord Shiva, earning the unusual form in which he is worshipped here. And while the idol predates the police station by centuries, it has remained within its compound since the new police station was built around 19 years ago."The idol was built by the local rulers around 300 years ago. My ancestors were Rajpurohits in the court of Kothi rulers and have been worshipping the idol since then. I remember at least four generations of my ancestors who performed the rituals. My father, grandfather and great-grandfather worshipped it on Dussehra, and now I carry on the tradition," said 56-year-old priest Ramesh Mishra.The tradition is rooted in local myth linking the region to the Ramayana.'More Ravana idols believed to exist' Mishra said he had heard from his forefathers that a small river once flowed near the idol, with a 'Ram Chabootra' on the opposite bank. The Kothi rulers would organise Ramlila there, during which Lord Rama would symbolically shoot arrows at Ravana's idol from across the river. A bridge over the water was said to represent Ram Setu, while the land on Ravana's side was known locally as 'Lanka'.Mishra also cited local lore about Ravana deploying informers along the borders of the forest where Lord Rama spent a considerable part of his life in Chitrakoot. He said similar Ravana idols were believed to exist in Chitrakoot and Pali in Umaria district.With Dussehra falling on Oct 20 in the region this year, Mishra and his family will once again perform the rituals at the idol - inside a police station that, unusually, safeguards a figure whom much of the country gathers to burn.The Kothi idol is not the only exception to the Dussehra tradition in Madhya Pradesh. In Vidisha district's Ravan village, devotees worship the demon king as 'Ravan Baba' and 'Kul Devta', with locals estimating that the reclining, 10-headed idol is over 500 years old; in Mandsaur's Khanpura, Ravana is revered as a son-in-law because Mandodari is believed to have belonged to the town.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: ‘Severe mental distress’: Gujarat man jumps off 1,700ft cliff, seeks changes to domestic violence laws in 13-min video
articles.summary: AHMEDABAD: A Gujarat postal employee allegedly died by suicide after jumping from the Konkankada cliff at Harishchandragad on Oct 12, leaving behind a
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: A Gujarat postal employee allegedly died by suicide after jumping from the Konkankada cliff at Harishchandragad on Oct 12, leaving behind a 13-minute video in which he cited distress linked to a matrimonial dispute and sought changes to laws governing such cases.Vishwaraj Gohil, a resident of Chitra in Bhavnagar and originally from Rajpara, allegedly jumped into the nearly 1,700-foot-deep gorge located on the border of Thane, Pune and Ahilyanagar districts.In the video, he spoke about his marital dispute, made allegations against his in-laws and urged authorities to review the implementation of laws related to domestic violence and matrimonial disputes. His allegations have not been independently verified.Also read: ‘They must prove I beat my wife’: Man 'begs' for justice in final video before suicideAccording to available information, Gohil married Dhaaraba Ajaysinh Sarvaiya on Feb 8, 2026. On Sep 12, his wife submitted an application to police alleging domestic violence following a marital dispute, prompting an inquiry. Gohil also appeared in court on Oct 9 in connection with the matter.In the video, Gohil said the dispute had caused him severe mental distress and alleged that his family had faced false accusations. He also raised concerns about reconciliation proceedings and a dispute involving jewellery.The incident came to light when passersby spotted a motorcycle and a mobile phone near the cliff and alerted Rajur police in Ahilyanagar district. Police contacted Gohil’s family, who reportedly informed them about the video they had received.Given the depth of the gorge, police deployed a drone camera to locate the body. A recovery operation with the assistance of mountaineers was carried out on Friday. The body was recovered after nearly 24 hours and later sent to Bhavnagar.As the spot where the body was found falls within the jurisdiction of Tokawade police station in Thane Rural, an accidental death report (ADR) was registered there.Shitalkumar Naik, assistant police inspector at Tokawade police station, said, “We have registered an ADR in the case. Further action will be taken based on the statements of family members and the findings of the investigation, including an examination of the video recorded by the deceased before his death.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.title: Meet Tim Armoo, the British entrepreneur who sold his first business at 17 for £110,000, lost the money within 15 months, then built another company that sold for eight figures
articles.summary: At 17, Tim Armoo had already experienced something many aspiring entrepreneurs spend years working towards.
articles.body: At 17, Tim Armoo had already experienced something many aspiring entrepreneurs spend years working towards. His first publishing business had attracted a buyer, bringing him £110,000 while he was still a teenager in south London. The money gave him an early taste of financial freedom, but it did not last. Within little more than a year, poor investment decisions had wiped out the proceeds. Armoo would eventually build another company, an influencer marketing agency that reached major brands and was sold for an eight-figure sum when he was 27. Between those two exits, however, he had to confront what his first success had taught him about money, risk and his own judgement.Tim Armoo built his first business as a teenager and sold it for £110,000 at 17In an interview with Fortune, Armoo revealed his entrepreneurial journey at 14, setting up a tutoring service that grew quickly. Within six weeks, he had expanded the operation to 65 tutors, giving him an early introduction to the practical demands of running a business. Finding customers, organising people and turning an idea into something that could grow were lessons he learnt well before most of his peers had considered a career.He went on to establish Entrepreneur Express, a publication that eventually attracted the attention of Horizon Media. The company was acquired for £110,000, a substantial sum for a teenager who had grown up in south London. It was his first meaningful business sale and a moment that changed his financial circumstances almost overnight.Armoo later recalled that he had struggled to appreciate the difference between achieving a successful exit and knowing how to manage the money that followed. He told Fortune, “That company got bought for £110,000. I’m this kid from like South London, I was like, bro, this is £110 million.”“So I got cocky, I got arrogant, and I started to invest it in stuff that I had absolutely zero clue about.”How overconfidence wiped out his £110,000 fortune before he turned 19“I thought I knew how to make money, and spread betting seemed like an easy way to make money… Silly. Within 12 to 15 months, all of it was gone.”Rather than preserving the proceeds or continuing to invest in businesses he understood, Armoo started looking for ways to make his money grow without having to build another company from scratch. He put money into a dental affiliate website, expecting it to become a profitable source of income. The venture failed to deliver the results he had anticipated.He then turned to spread betting, a form of financial speculation in which people wager on price movements. Armoo approached it with the confidence of someone who had already made money through entrepreneurship, although the skills required were very different. His earlier success had encouraged him to believe that making money was something he could repeat almost at will.Looking back, Armoo attributed the loss to overconfidence and arrogance. He had mistaken an early business achievement for evidence that he could succeed in unfamiliar financial markets. The experience marked a difficult reversal. He had moved from earning a significant sum as a teenager to having none of that money left before he was 19.Building Fanbytes into an eight-figure business and securing a second exitArmoo returned to the activity that had brought him his first success: building a business. In 2017, during his second year at university, he founded Fanbytes, an influencer marketing agency focused on helping brands reach audiences through social media.The company developed as influencer marketing became an increasingly important part of how businesses communicated with younger consumers. Its growth eventually attracted Brainlabs, the digital marketing group that acquired Fanbytes in 2022. The deal was reported as an eight-figure sale, making Armoo 27 at the time of his second major exit.Entrepreneur Express had provided an early financial breakthrough, but the proceeds disappeared before he reached adulthood. Fanbytes was built over several years and developed into an agency with established clients before its acquisition. This time, his wealth came from a business he had spent years growing rather than a series of attempts to make money through unfamiliar investments.The hidden emotional cost of selling his company for millionsSelling Fanbytes brought Armoo another substantial financial reward, but it also introduced a problem he had not anticipated. For roughly six months after the acquisition, he felt on top of the world. Then the excitement faded, leaving him uncertain about what to do next.Before selling the company, Armoo had dismissed accounts from entrepreneurs who described feeling empty after a major business exit. He believed that having millions of pounds in the bank should be enough to remove such feelings. Once he experienced the transition himself, he began to understand why some founders struggled after leaving the businesses that had occupied so much of their lives.For years, his routine had revolved around building a company, pursuing growth and working towards a sale. Once that objective had been achieved, the structure that had organised his time and given him a sense of purpose was no longer there in the same form.Armoo described spending around two years grappling with the question of what came next. He later said, “I had to work really hard to not tie who I was to my achievements,” Armoo said, while adding that it took around a year to separate his big win from his ego. “That was a big thing… I had to go through quite a lot of mental change, psychological change.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Kim Jong Un photos released to dismiss rumours of coma, takeover by sister
articles.summary: North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after
articles.body: North Korean supreme leader Kim Jong Un has resurfaced in photographs released by state media, inspecting children's footwear and women's clothing, after unverified claims circulated online that he had died from a brain haemorrhage.The photographs, published by North Korea's official media on Monday, show Kim examining footwear, gesturing towards officials and inspecting coats at a garment and footwear exhibition. The images emerged amid a wave of social media speculation about the 42-year-old leader's health and the possibility of a succession crisis in the secretive country, the New York Post reported.According to North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency, Kim toured the exhibition on Monday. However, the photographs have not been independently authenticated, and it remains unclear precisely when they were taken.One image shows Kim bending forward to inspect a small pink shoe held by a woman. In another, he gestures with his arms outstretched as he appears to address an official. A third photograph captures him reaching towards the sleeve of a woman's coat displayed on a mannequin.How the death rumours beganThe speculation gathered pace after Wanjun Xie, a US-based Chinese dissident associated with the China Democracy Party, posted a series of claims on X alleging that Kim had died and that his sister, Kim Yo Jong, had taken control of the country.In a post on Monday, Xie wrote: "Rumours of the death of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un have been circulating online for days, but Kim Jong Un has not yet made a public appearance to deny them. This indirectly confirms that the rumours of Kim Jong Un's death are likely true. Furthermore, it is rumoured that after Kim Jong-un's death, the North Korean regime has not been transferred to his daughter Kim Ju-ae, but is currently in the hands of his sister Kim Yo-jong."After assuming power, Kim Yo-jong immediately activated loudspeaker broadcasts to South Korea and fired 201 warning shots. She also warned South Korea that North Korea was considering a comprehensive upgrade of its tactical strike capabilities. This sudden intensification of threats against South Korea is clearly aimed at strengthening her control over the North Korean military and consolidating her power through strong external threats. This indirectly confirms the rumors that Kim Jong-un is dead and that Kim Yo-jong is currently in control of the regime; these rumors are likely true."The New York Post reported that Xie's claims began gaining traction on Sunday. However, the allegations have not been supported by medical records, identifiable witnesses or other independently verifiable evidence.In another post on Sunday, Xie claimed that Kim had suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage, fallen into a coma and been transferred to Beijing for emergency treatment. He alleged that a team of specialists from Peking Union Medical College Hospital had travelled to North Korea before Kim was moved to China."It is rumoured that recently, Kim Jong-un, General Secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and Supreme Leader of North Korea, suffered a severe cerebral haemorrhage and fell into a coma. Although a team of medical experts from Peking Union Medical College Hospital was dispatched to North Korea to assist in his treatment, the poor medical conditions in North Korea forced Kim Jong-un to be transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment. However, due to the severity of his condition and the fact that the optimal window for treatment had passed, Kim Jong-un succumbed to his injuries and died. His body has been secretly transported back to North Korea, and the news of his death is being kept under wraps."Xie further alleged that Kim's body had been secretly returned to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death. He also claimed that Chinese troops had been deployed to Pyongyang amid fears of a succession crisis.In a separate post, he wrote: "It is said that on October 17, Peking Union Medical College Hospital dispatched a team of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular medical experts to North Korea to participate in the rescue of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, who was in critical condition."Claims of Chinese troop deploymentXie's posts also fuelled speculation about a possible power struggle involving Kim's daughter, Kim Ju-ae, and his sister, Kim Yo Jong. He claimed that China had sent 9,000 troops to Pyongyang to help stabilise the situation.The claims of Kim's death, a Chinese troop deployment and a possible succession crisis remain unverified. North Korean authorities have not explicitly addressed the death reports.What is known about Kim's health?Kim's health has long been the subject of international speculation. The New York Post reported that South Korea's National Intelligence Service told lawmakers on September 30 that Kim weighed approximately 140 kilograms (309 pounds) and faced an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease because of severe obesity.However, the agency reportedly detected no significant signs of ill health, pointing to Kim's ability to run up stairs during an inspection of a naval destroyer.The latest rumours echo a false alarm in 2020, when Ji Seong-ho, a North Korean defector who later became a South Korean lawmaker, claimed he was "99%" certain that Kim had died following cardiovascular surgery. Kim subsequently appeared in public, and Ji apologised for making the erroneous claim.The New York Post said it had sought comment from the governments of North Korea and China, as well as Peking Union Medical College Hospital.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bangladesh Hindu group condemns sealing of historic Ram Leela Temple in Pakistan
articles.summary: Bangladesh Hindu Sammilon Sangho has expressed concern and strongly condemned the sealing of the centuries-old Ramlila Temple in Dera Ismail Khan, in
articles.body: Bangladesh Hindu Sammilon Sangho has expressed concern and strongly condemned the sealing of the centuries-old Ramlila Temple in Dera Ismail Khan, in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, amid reports of plans to demolish the historic structure and build a commercial complex on the site.In a statement issued on Saturday, the organisation said the reported move violated religious freedom and basic human rights. It also expressed solidarity with the local Hindu community and civil society members opposing the proposed construction."Our organisation, which firmly believes in the non-communal spirit of the great Liberation War, equality, and the core mantra of religious freedom, considers any attempt to destroy or force the closure of a place of worship to be a grave violation of basic human rights and freedom of religion", Bangladesh Hindu Sammilon Sangha said in a statement.According to media reports, the plan to demolish the historic temple and build a commercial building on its site was deeply tragic and contrary to global communal harmony."We extend our solidarity and full support to the brave resistance mounted by the local Hindu community and members of civil society against this attempt to destroy the historic structure", it added.The organisation urged the Pakistani government to protect the temple, stop any attempt to build a commercial complex at the site and restore the community’s right to conduct religious practices and rituals there. It also called for action against those responsible."We call upon the Government of Pakistan to immediately ensure the security of this historic and traditional temple, permanently halt all attempts to build a commercial complex, and restore the right to conduct religious practices and rituals at the location. At the same time, we demand exemplary punishment for those identified behind this heinous incident", the statement said."We also humbly request the international community to raise a stronger voice to protect minority rights and religious freedom in every corner of the world", it said.Earlier on Sunday, authorities in Dera Ismail Khan sealed the historic Ram Leela Temple in Rahim Bazaar, raising concerns over the protection of religious heritage and the proposed conversion of the site into a commercial property.The move came days after civil society activists intervened to prevent the building’s demolition for a commercial plaza, Dawn reported.According to the report, the temple had earlier been sealed by Assistant Commissioner Hamid Siddiq following public protests, and construction work at the site had been halted.The latest sealing has renewed concerns among residents and heritage advocates about the future of the historic structure. The development coincided with a joint meeting of civil society representatives and members of the Hindu community to discuss the reported demolition plans. Participants opposed the proposed commercial construction and urged elected representatives to raise the issue in Pakistan’s national assembly.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2022, a fourth-generation Colorado farming family sold 90 acres to Xcel Energy for $585,000; four years later, the utility sought a 550-foot easement for $19,000, but a judge rejected its condemnation bid
articles.summary: A dispute over a narrow strip of ranchland in eastern Colorado has become a broader legal battle over how far an electricity utility can go to secure land
articles.body: A dispute over a narrow strip of ranchland in eastern Colorado has become a broader legal battle over how far an electricity utility can go to secure land for renewable energy projects. According to reporting by The Colorado Sun, Utility Dive and the Kiowa County Independent, Xcel Energy is challenging a ruling that denied it the power to seize a disputed easement from a fourth-generation farming and ranching family. The conflict centres on Dryland Partners, a family-run agricultural business operated by Darin Dickey and his brothers in Cheyenne County. The family had sold approximately 90 acres to Xcel Energy in 2022 for $585,000 to accommodate the Goose Creek substation. However, negotiations later broke down over a separate 550-foot right of way needed to connect two wind farms to the electricity grid.In June 2026, Cheyenne County District Judge Mike Davidson rejected the utility’s condemnation petition, finding that it lacked the authority to acquire the land through eminent domain for the proposed generation tie lines. The judge also determined that the utility had acted in bad faith by pursuing a route that would cause unnecessary harm to the landowners despite the availability of less damaging alternatives.A disagreement over the route and compensationXcel Energy, through its subsidiary Public Service Company of Colorado, proposed routing the power lines across the intersection of County Roads DD and 36 before connecting them to the Goose Creek substation.The Dickey family objected to this alignment, citing potential safety concerns for heavy agricultural machinery and possible interference with an existing natural gas pipeline right of way. The family proposed alternative routes that it said would reduce disruption to its farming operations. The utility offered $19,000 for the easement, an amount the family considered inadequate compared with compensation negotiated for a separate wind energy connection at the same substation. Dryland Partners had previously reached an agreement with NextEra Energy Resources to connect its Dusty Rose wind farm to the facility.Xcel maintained that its offer exceeded fair market value and argued that the family’s alternative proposals would involve prohibitively expensive changes. The disagreement over compensation, however, is only one part of the case. The central legal question is whether a regulated utility can use eminent domain to obtain land for generation tie lines that connect individual power plants to the grid.Why the disputed power lines matterThe easement is required for two wind projects, Singing Grass and Cheyenne Ridge II, which have a combined planned generating capacity of approximately 1,053 megawatts. The projects are intended to connect to the Goose Creek substation and subsequently feed electricity into Xcel’s $1.7 billion Power Pathway transmission network.The distinction between transmission infrastructure and generation tie lines is central to the dispute. While utilities have established authority to acquire certain land for public transmission infrastructure, the family argued that the disputed connections primarily serve individual generating facilities rather than directly delivering electricity to consumers. The ruling could therefore have implications beyond the Dickey family’s property, potentially influencing how renewable energy developers secure land for connections to the wider electricity network.Colorado Supreme Court declines an early interventionXcel sought to have the Colorado Supreme Court consider the case directly, arguing that the dispute raised important questions about renewable energy development and the utility’s condemnation powers. However, on August 31, 2026, the state’s highest court declined to take up the case through this expedited route. The decision did not resolve the underlying legal questions. Xcel said it would continue with its appeal before the Colorado Court of Appeals.The utility has argued that the unresolved easement is delaying the completion of infrastructure needed to bring the two wind farms online. The family, meanwhile, has maintained that it remains willing to negotiate a solution using alternative routes and reasonable terms. The outcome will determine more than the location of a power line across an agricultural property. It could also help clarify the limits of eminent domain when utilities seek land to connect privately developed or utility-owned renewable energy projects to the grid.You use AI every day. articles.title: America's largest bank CEO Jamie Dimon makes it clear at earnings call that not giving AI Agents access to bank's data; calls it too risky for clients and JPMorgan
articles.summary: Jamie Dimon the CEO of America's largest bank JPMorgan Chase has made it clear that the bank will not allow external artificial intelligence agents to
articles.body: Jamie Dimon the CEO of America's largest bank JPMorgan Chase has made it clear that the bank will not allow external artificial intelligence agents to access customer accounts and carry out actions on the behalf of users, warning that the technology presently poses significant risks for both customers and bank. According to a report by CNBC, speaking during the bank’s third-quarter earnings call, Dimon said JPMorgan Chase is taking a cautious approach as technology companies including Meta roll out increasingly autonomous AI assistants. "We're not going to allow just any ... outside agent to come in inside the company, because it's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," Dimon told analysts. Dimon further added that the possibility of large numbers of autonomous agents interacting with banking systems raises security concerns. "You don't want rogue agents, and it could be thousands of them," Dimon saidBank blocks AI agents from taking actions confirms JPMorganA JPMorgan spokesperson confirmed to CNBC that the bank currently prevents external AI agents from operating customer accounts. According to the bank, third parties are not permitted to gain access by using customers' banking credentials and logging in on their behalf.While AI agents can access some account information in a read-only format through open banking providers and data connectors, they cannot carry out transactions such as sending money, moving funds or paying bills.The bank said it supports customer-authorised data sharing through open banking services and is working toward enabling agentic connections securely, but has not provided a timeline for allowing third-party AI agents to directly interact with customer accounts.‘Liability transfer’Dimon said JPMorgan is using AI agents internally and plans to deploy them in customer-facing applications. He said the bank’s approach is not about being for or against the technology, but about making sure it serves customers safely. He also drew a line on liability when customers authorize outside agents to act for them. “If people are using them, they should understand the risk,” Dimon said. “They should understand there’s a liability transfer.”Defensive move: Smart CashIn recent weeks, JPMorgan began a targeted pilot of its own AI tool, Smart Cash, Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum said Tuesday. It aims to predict a user’s cash flow and move funds to maximize yield. That would appear to be a defensive move against external agents.Why banks are nervousPersonal AI agents have gained mainstream popularity in recent months as models gain more autonomy, such as the ability to cancel subscriptions or use credit cards for a user. Instinct, a text-message-based digital concierge, launched earlier this year on an invitation-only basis. Its maker, San Francisco-based Spear Street Technology, was founded last year and reached a $10 billion valuation last month.In September, bank stocks fell after Meta’s Muse agent topped app download charts soon after its unveiling. Investors feared consumers would use agents to move funds from low-yielding accounts to higher-yielding ones. Weeks later, OpenAI released its own agent, Dots.Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok and others have pointed to the risks such agents pose to cheap bank deposits. That risk would be limited, though, if agents are not allowed to operate freely in customers’ accounts.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1980, a signed Hockney print went inside Paper Pools; 46 years later, Norwich volunteer Jemma Banks found it, and the Salvation Army raised £41,160
articles.summary: A signed print by David Hockney, hidden for 46 years inside a donated copy of Paper Pools, was discovered by volunteer Jemma Banks in Norwich and sold for £41,160, benefiting the Salvation Army's community work.
articles.body: A signed print that was created by British artist David Hockney was sold for £41,160 after a volunteer discovered it inside a donated copy of Paper Pools at a Salvation Army charity shop in Norwich, England. Jemma Banks is a long-serving volunteer and local artist who spotted the print while examining the book at the shop on Goat Lane. The publication had been donated in 2025, and the artwork had remained inside it for 46 years, with the Salvation Army subsequently listing the item through its Collectables & Curiosity eBay shop. The winning bidder chose to remain anonymous, and paid more than £41,000 for the find, with the charity confirming that the proceeds would support its community work.A donated book contained an original signed printBanks recognised that the donated publication might be valuable when she examined it at the shop and she found an original print bearing Hockney's signature inside, with the artwork remaining tucked between the pages rather than being displayed or stored separately. The Salvation Army Trading Company researched the item before it was listed for sale online, after which bidding gathered pace, and the final price reached £41,160. The charity did not disclose the winning bidder's identity.The buyer told the Salvation Army that he had admired Hockney's work for many years, and had also welcomed the opportunity to support the charity through the purchase. Banks said that she had been amazed that the print had remained inside the book for so long, and described it as looking as fresh as when it came off the lithographic press. Her experience as a local artist helped her recognise that the donation needed to be examined closely, although she had not expected the eventual sale price. Major Tracey Bale leads the Salvation Army's Norwich Citadel, and credits Banks's knowledge with helping the organisation identify the artwork.How Hockney Made Paper PoolsHockney's Paper Pools series started with experiments on colored paper pulp rather than conventional ink, and he worked with printmaker Kenneth Tyler at Tyler Graphics in New York during 1978 and 1979, with paper pulp being used to build images of swimming pools, reflections and water. The process involved placing colored paper pulp into molds, then pressing and drying it to form the finished works, and Hockney used the method to create different textures and color effects. Paper Pools was published in 1980 and became one of his notable experiments in printmaking.What was inside Paper Pools?Hockney's Paper Pools was published in 1980, and the book is associated with the artist's work that involved swimming pools and paper pulp, which was a subject he explored during his career in painting and printmaking. His official bibliography lists Paper Pools among his publications for 1980, alongside David Hockney: 23 Lithographs 1978–1980, which was published by Tyler Graphics Ltd. Hockney’s work spanned painting, drawing, photography and printmaking, and his pool imagery became an important part of his career, and prints that were produced in editions could circulate among collectors, while individual copies might remain in private collections for decades.Hockney died at home on June 11, 2026, aged 88, according to ITV News Anglia, with the auction taking place the following month, although the reporting does not establish whether his death affected the bidding. articles.title: Meet Cliver Huamán: At 15, turned away from South America’s biggest club soccer final, he climbed a hill, called the match and drew thousands of live viewers
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring story of Cliver Huamán, a 15-year-old commentator from Peru who climbed a hill to broadcast the Copa Libertadores final, reaching nearly 47,000 live viewers. Learn how his journey began and the impact of live streaming in sports.
articles.body: Many of the biggest games in South American football draw far more spectators outside the stadiums than inside them. Fans watch on television and radio and, increasingly, on social media, where anyone with a mobile phone and a microphone can build an audience. One such commentator is Cliver Huamán Sánchez, a teenager from Huampica, in the Andes of Peru, who narrates football matches online under the name Pol Deportes. For the Copa Libertadores final in Lima, he travelled from his home region to cover the match live. He was not allowed into the stadium and instead narrated it from a nearby hill.Cliver Huamán began narrating matches online about four years before the 2025 finalCliver Huamán Sánchez, from Huampica in Andahuaylas, Peru, began posting match videos online about four years before the 2025 final, Caretas reported. His older brother, Kenny, persuaded him to build his own channels, and his father had taken him to a local radio station as a child, according to a BBC Mundo interview republished by Observador in Costa Rica. Bluewin, a Swiss news site, adds that the family grows kiwicha and quinoa.He traveled 16 to 18 hours and was unable to get accreditation for the November 29, 2025 finalAccording to a December 1, 2025 TUDN report, Cliver Huamán could not get press credentials for the Copa Libertadores final because he was 15 and not yet an adult. Reports differ on the length of the trip from Andahuaylas: Reuters and We Are Mitú give 18 hours, while Bluewin and BBC Mundo give 16 hours. NTN24 reported that Flamengo won 1–0 against Palmeiras at the Estadio Monumental in Lima on November 29, 2025, winning the Copa Libertadores. Huamán climbed Cerro Puruchuco, an Inca archaeological site east of Lima, as El País describes it. El Litoral and NTN24 report that he set up a phone, ring light, tripod and microphone, put on a suit and tie, and streamed live on TikTok while his brother produced.Reports put his peak concurrent audience between 10,000 and 47,000 viewersFutbolPeruano.com reports that he provided commentary for the full 90 minutes and drew an audience of 47,000, along with more than one million followers. Ecuador’s Extra reported on December 3, 2025 that Huamán described his livestream growing from 30 viewers to 400, then 5,000 and then 10,000. Estimates of his audience therefore range from 10,000 concurrent viewers to 47,000 at peak.Live streaming research offers context for the audience he reachedA 2020 study of live-streaming viewers in China offers some context for the audience he reached, although it does not cover football in Latin America. InWho Watches Live Streaming in China? Examining Viewers’ Behaviors, Personality Traits, and Motivations, published in Frontiers in Psychology, Yi Xu and Yixin Ye identified social interaction, information gathering, and entertainment as the main motivations for watching live streams, and found that those motivations were linked to how often viewers watched and which genres they chose. Extraversion was negatively associated with live streaming use, while openness was positively associated.A second paper, Motivations for the Use of Video Game Streaming Platforms: The Moderating Effect of Sex, Age and Self-Perception of Level as a Player, appeared in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. In the study, the authors modelled 338 valid responses and found that the three motivation constructs explained 70.8% of the variance in use, with an SRMR below 0.10 indicating acceptable fit. They also report that sex and age did not moderate the motivation- use relationship, whereas self-perceived player level did, so hypotheses 4 and 5 were rejected.Television invitations in Lima and Madrid followed the broadcastL1 MAX, which holds the broadcasting rights for the Sporting Cristal-Alianza Lima playoff, invited Huamán to narrate part of the match at Lima’s Estadio Nacional, Panamericana reported. Latina Television then invited him to travel to Spain to cover the Champions League match between Real Madrid and Manchester City, We Are Mitú reported, and Caretas says he hopes to win a scholarship to study journalism and communication.You use AI every day. articles.title: In a solar-simulator test, aluminum cooling fins raised a panel’s output 11.5%; adding folded plastic bags lifted the increase only slightly, to 11.6%
articles.summary: Discover how researchers enhanced solar panel output by 11.6% using a combination of aluminum cooling fins and repurposed plastic bags in a groundbreaking laboratory experiment.
articles.body: Solar panels can lose some of their electrical performance as they heat up under strong sunlight. Scientists have tried several ways to limit heat on panels without electric cooling, including using affordable materials that would normally be thrown away. One study used a cheap combination of aluminum heat sinks and folded plastic bags mounted on the rear of a solar panel. These results suggest that a non-electric cooling system can improve solar panel performance, at least under laboratory conditions. Discarded plastic bags could thus have another application in managing heat.Aluminum fins helped release heat from the panelA 2019 study by Ammar Alkhalidi, Mohamad K. Khawaja and Abdel Ghaffar Al Kelany, Investigation of Repurposed Material Utilization for Environmental Protection and Reduction of Overheat Power Losses in PV Panels, published in the International Journal of Photoenergy, examined whether repurposed plastic materials could help cool photovoltaic panels and reduce heat-related power losses. The researchers tested the panel under halogen-lamp simulator conditions, then added fitted heat-extraction fins before layering in repurposed HDPE and plastic bags.They report that this passive cooling approach lowered panel temperature and raised power output at 1000 W m⁻², with the perforated fin design chosen for its lower weight and better airflow. The perforated aluminum fins were attached to the back of the panel to increase its surface area for heat exchange, and the perforations let air move through them. No fans or pumps were used because the cooling method was passive.Aluminum fins and folded plastic bags increased output power by 11.6%The biggest performance increase came from combining aluminum cooling fins with folded plastic bags on the back of the panel. At a simulated irradiance of 1,000 watts per square metre, this configuration produced 11.6% more output power than the unmodified panel and lowered the panel’s temperature by 22.7%. Aluminum fins alone raised output power by 11.5%, so the bags added only a small further gain. The study also tested the fins with ground HDPE, but the highest output came from the folded plastic bags.Lower panel temperatures can improve electrical performanceHeat management matters because photovoltaic modules generally lose electrical performance as their operating temperature rises. The review On the temperature dependence of photovoltaic module electrical performance: A review of efficiency/power correlations by E. Skoplaki and J. A. Palyvos, published in Solar Energy in 2009, examines the relationship between module temperature, electrical efficiency, and power output. In the opinion of the authors, the review is dedicated to one-sun commercial silicon modules and considers how temperature affects the major electrical characteristics, particularly efficiency and maximum power. The review also emphasizes the typical test condition of 25°C and 1000 W/m² and explains the temperature effect using the well-known negative temperature coefficient.The energy production of solar panels requires sunlight, but the heat caused by high irradiance lowers their voltage and peak power. Thus, removal of excessive heat could enable a panel to produce more efficient electric energy using the same amount of sunlight. In the above-mentioned study by Alkhalidi and colleagues, the possibility was tested with a passive cooling system made of aluminum fins and plastic. Since this system did not use any equipment for active cooling, it had the potential to increase the efficiency of panels without requiring additional electricity consumption. But the observed effect was reached only in a laboratory setting, not necessarily reflecting results that could be achieved in outdoor installations due to variations in sunlight, air moisture, and wind.Outdoor testing is needed to establish practical benefitsThe combination of these materials with aluminum fins represents a simple way of temperature control and reuse of waste material. There are some practical issues that need to be investigated. For example, how does the change of outdoor conditions such as varying light, wind, dust, and humidity influence the cooling process? The researchers should study the system's durability, maintenance, and costs of its installation before determining its feasibility. This experiment showed that a passive cooling system using aluminum fins and folded plastic bags can increase a solar panel’s power under laboratory conditions.You use AI every day. articles.body: A protester demanding the release of the Jeffrey Epstein files interrupted US Vice-President JD Vance’s speech on Monday at a Republican campaign rally in Hendersonville, North Carolina, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.Just few minutes into Vance’s address, a man standing directly behind the vice-president stood up and shouted, “God bless our children!” and “Release the Epstein files”, footage of the incident showed. Security personnel subsequently escorted the protester out as he continued shouting.The interruption brought renewed attention to the Trump administration’s handling of records relating to Epstein, the disgraced financier and convicted sex offender whose sexual abuse of underage girls and connections to powerful figures have fuelled years of scrutiny.According to footage of the rally, Vance joked after the protester was removed by referring to his earlier remarks on illegal border crossings. “I said that we have had zero illegal border crossings in the United States of America, but one isn’t bad right?” he said.The Epstein files comprise investigative records, court documents, emails, photographs, videos and other material relating to Epstein, his associates and investigations into his activities.On January 30, 2026, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) announced the release of more than three million additional pages, bringing the total disclosure to nearly 3.5 million pages. The records include investigative material, court documents, communications and information about Epstein’s associates. Being named in the files does not, by itself, establish criminal wrongdoing.Vance acknowledged the administration’s communication problems over the disclosures in July, saying it had “absolutely screwed up the comms”, according to his remarks on a podcast. He blamed former attorney-general Pam Bondi for overstating what the initial releases contained, while denying that the administration was deliberately concealing information.The controversy has persisted amid questions about redactions and whether all relevant records have been disclosed. articles.title: In 2001, a former Illinois quarry where solvents and paint were dumped opened as a forest preserve with a 115-acre lake, an education centre, and an amphitheatre
articles.summary: Discover how the former Petersen Sand and Gravel quarry in Libertyville, Illinois, transformed from a hazardous waste site to the beautiful Independence Grove Forest Preserve, featuring a 115-acre lake, an education center, and an amphitheatre.
articles.body: Old gravel pits are a common sight in the American Midwest. When the sand and stone are exhausted, they often are left as deep pits with steep walls, and some of them silently turn into dumping places. It’s not often you get a second life as a spot where families swim, rent boats and set up on a lawn for summer concerts.That’s what happened at the former Petersen Sand and Gravel quarry in Libertyville, Lake County, Illinois. Once the barrels of paint and solvent waste were excavated and hauled away and the federal and state agencies decided no additional cleanup was necessary, the Lake County Forest Preserve District completed the conversion of the pit into Independence Grove Forest Preserve. It opened to the public in spring 2001 with a lake of 115 acres, a visitor centre and an amphitheatre.From gravel pit to disposal siteAccording to an EPA fact sheet on reuse, the quarry was in operation from 1952 to 1971. By the time it closed, much of the topsoil was gone, and the sides had vertical walls of up to 60 feet high. It would be a tough place to adore, but the Lake County Forest Preserve District purchased the area in 1979 and began designing a preserve around it.The pit’s darker history began when its owner, Raymond Petersen, let people deposit waste in a worked-out corner from the mid-1950s, state records show. Nobody knows when the paint, the paint debris and the solvents started coming. Petersen was refused a permit for a landfill in 1971, and the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency investigated allegations of illegal dumping and ordered it stopped. Between 400 and 500 drums of paint and solvent waste were removed in 1977.Later, there were more. Lake County Grading, the mining firm the district had contracted to regrade the pit in exchange for the remaining gravel, found hidden drums while regrading in 1983. That year, a forest preserve district contractor removed contaminated soil and about 500 drums of solvents and 1,000 paint cans.Checking the siteThe pit was included on the federal Superfund National Priorities List in 1986, and the Illinois EPA, with help from the US EPA, conducted a detailed examination. Fieldwork was carried out between October 1986 and December 1987, with the final report submitted in April 1988. Investigators took samples of groundwater, soil, surface water and sediment. They analysed groundwater for more than 150 compounds, and only iron and manganese went above drinking water guidelines set for taste and odour, a level that was also exceeded in groundwater upgradient of the site. Soil showed low levels of a few solvents, such as toluene, plus traces of pesticides and one low reading of PCBs.Investigators were also keen to make sure no more drums were hidden. They took soil borings at the three known dumping areas and 23 other locations and did buried metal surveys over a 20-acre grid. Nothing came up.A 1988 EPA document summed up the findings: the earlier waste removals had been enough to protect people and the environment, and no unacceptable danger remained, so no further cleanup was required. There was one requirement. Because no one could accurately predict conditions once a lake filled the pit, the agencies asked the county to monitor surface water and sediment before and after the lake was formed. The facility was removed off the Superfund list in 1991.Creating the lake and the preserveThe district signed an agreement with Lake County Grading to regrade and restore the property in exchange for mining the remaining gravel. What began as plans for walks, picnicking, swimming and boating expanded to include a visitor centre, a marina complex, a cafe, an event pavilion, an amphitheatre and a native plant garden. While mining continued, crews pumped around 1.7 million gallons of water a night from a sump pond into the neighbouring Des Plaines River to keep the pit dry. The pit floor sat about 20 feet below the river level, so it had to be pumped dry for mining to continue.When the work was done, the 120-acre former quarry site formed part of a forest preserve of more than 1,100 acres, centred on a 115-acre lake. The visitor centre covers 19,000 square feet and hosts changing exhibits. The preserve also features a marina with boat rentals, a beach, catch-and-release fishing, miles of trails and guided night hikes with naturalists. The amphitheatre hosts an annual summer concert series next to a fountain and native garden.As of 2007, the site had not had any further environmental problems since it was redeveloped, and a visitor would be hard-pressed to tell that the lake sits in a former quarry and garbage dumping area, the fact sheet says. The lesson from Libertyville is not that of a magical cleanup but of patience, testing and monitoring that allowed a ruined gravel pit to become a lake that visitors today use for swimming, boating and fishing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jensen Huang and his wife donated $75 million to Vanderbilt; the gift helped push funding for its planned San Francisco campus past $100 million
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, have donated $75 million to Vanderbilt University to help establish a new college focused on art,
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, have donated $75 million to Vanderbilt University to help establish a new college focused on art, architecture and design at its planned San Francisco campus. Announced on July 21, 2026, the gift has helped attract additional contributions, taking total philanthropic support for the campus beyond $100 million, according to the university. The donation will establish the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design, which is intended to bring creative disciplines together with technology, engineering and entrepreneurship. The campus is expected to open in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, and will build on the legacy of the California College of the Arts.How the $75 million donation pushed Vanderbilt's campus funding past $100 millionThe Huang family's contribution is structured as a matching gift, designed to encourage other donors to support the university's expansion in San Francisco. Vanderbilt said the donation had already generated further philanthropic commitments from alumni and other supporters, taking the total investment in the campus beyond $100 million.Among the early supporters named by the university are Katie and Matt Paige, Jeff and Marieke Rothschild, and Leah and Ben Spero. The fundraising effort also includes significant commitments from anonymous donors and members of the Bay Area's arts and creative communities.Vanderbilt said it had secured more than 40% of the funding needed to realise the full match by December 31, 2028. The commitments will support the establishment and operation of the new college, along with additional academic programmes planned for the campus.Why the new college will combine art with technologyThe Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design is intended to make creative disciplines central to Vanderbilt's San Francisco campus. Its proposed academic model will combine studio practice and design labs with technical education, engineering and entrepreneurship.The university plans to offer undergraduate and graduate programmes, as well as community arts, pre-collegiate and lifelong-learning opportunities. These programmes remain subject to the necessary academic reviews and regulatory approvals.Huang explained the thinking behind the contribution in Vanderbilt's announcement, saying, “Technology expands what we can build. Art and design determine why we build it. Together they shape civilization.”The initiative reflects the family's stated belief that artistic creativity and design are important to technological progress, business innovation and the cultural life of a city.Vanderbilt plans to open its San Francisco campus in 2027The university expects the new campus to serve approximately 1,000 undergraduate and graduate students, alongside full-time faculty and staff. It is part of Vanderbilt's wider expansion beyond its main campus in Nashville, Tennessee.The San Francisco project will build on the nearly 120-year legacy of the California College of the Arts (CCA). Vanderbilt and CCA have agreed that CCA will contribute its campus to Vanderbilt after its operations wind down, subject to customary regulatory and other transaction requirements.Vanderbilt also plans to establish the California College of the Arts Institute to preserve and extend CCA's artistic and cultural legacy. The proposed institute will include the Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts, preserve and digitise CCA's archives, and support artists, designers, architects, curators and scholars through fellowships and residencies.The university has begun a national search for the founding dean of the new college. Its opening remains dependent on the required approvals, with the first students expected in 2027.The Huangs have also backed scientific and AI researchThe Vanderbilt contribution is separate from another philanthropic initiative involving the couple. In May 2026, Reuters reported that the foundation run by Jensen and Lori Huang had purchased computing time from CoreWeave and donated it to universities and nonprofit institutions for scientific and artificial intelligence research.A regulatory filing valued the computing resources donated through that initiative at $108.3 million. Nvidia also planned to provide free engineering services to some recipients.The arrangement involved CoreWeave, a cloud computing company that uses Nvidia-designed graphics processing units for AI workloads. Reuters noted that Nvidia had invested $2 billion in CoreWeave and agreed to purchase $6.3 billion in cloud capacity from the company, relationships that had raised investor concerns about potential circular financing.The computing donation and the Vanderbilt gift serve different purposes. The former supports research infrastructure, while the latter backs a new academic institution intended to connect art, design and technology in San Francisco.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1972, Phoenix sealed Sky Harbor's main runway with tire-rubber beside an untreated taxiway; 13 years later, untreated asphalt hardened 20 times more and cracked
articles.summary: Discover the benefits of asphalt-rubber sealing at Sky Harbor International Airport, revealing how treated surfaces significantly reduced asphalt aging and cracking compared to untreated sections.
articles.body: Phoenix treated the main runway at Sky Harbor International Airport with an asphalt-rubber seal in June 1972 and left the taxiway adjacent to it untreated. The asphalt beneath the untreated taxiway had hardened more than 20 times as much as the asphalt protected by the rubber seal, which was the result of thirteen years of pavement sampling. Russell Howard Schnormeier, who was an engineer with the City of Phoenix, documented the comparison in a 1986 paper that was published in Transportation Research Record, with the two surfaces using otherwise identical asphaltic concrete. The main runway received a stress-absorbing membrane, or SAM, that was made from asphalt-rubber and small stone chips, while the adjacent taxiway did not receive the treatment.Researchers collected pavement cores from the runway and taxiway at intervals between 1972 and 1985, and then measured the viscosity of the asphalt cement that had been recovered. Viscosity is a measure of a material's resistance to flow, and changes in asphalt viscosity can help indicate how much the binder has hardened with age.The rubber seal limited asphalt hardeningThe 1985 measurements showed a substantial difference between the two surfaces, with one comparison showing that asphalt from the treated runway had a viscosity of 1,125 poises at 140°F, while the untreated taxiway's asphalt measured 92,500 poises; another comparison recorded more than 200,000 poises in the untreated section, compared with 1,411 poises in the treated section. Schnormeier reported that the untreated asphalt had undergone more than 20 times as much hardening from oxidation and weathering, and the asphalt beneath the rubber seal showed no increase in viscosity that could be appreciated over the 13-year period.The difference was attributed to the seal's ability to limit the loss and reaction of volatile components in the asphalt, with the untreated material becoming brittle and cracked, while the treated surface was able to retain more of its flexibility. The paper also reported that crack reflection was prevented and surface maintenance had been eliminated for 13 years, although the runway required periodic high-pressure water cleaning to remove rubber buildup from aircraft tires. The test measured the properties of asphalt recovered from pavement cores, and not just the visible condition of the runway, with the viscosity measurements providing a numerical comparison of how the binder aged under the two treatments.How recycled tire rubber works in pavementAsphalt-rubber is made by blending asphalt cement with ground tire rubber, and the Federal Highway Administration explains that crumb rubber can modify the binder's properties, including its elasticity and resistance to aging. A stress-absorbing membrane is formed by applying hot asphalt-rubber and covering it with aggregate chips, and when it is used on an existing pavement, the layer can seal the surface and reduce the reflection of smaller cracks through the treatment. Its performance depends on the condition of the underlying structure and the way the treatment is installed, and does not eliminate every type of pavement failure.A 1991 study by Equbalali Charania, Joe A. Cano, and Schnormeier reviewed the city's wider experience with the material, which included its use on streets and at Sky Harbor, and described the treatment's ability to retard cracking and preserve asphalt properties, while noting that the performance varied with pavement conditions and construction details. The airport comparison is still a very specific example of the treatment's reported effect on asphalt aging, and after 13 years, the treated runway's asphalt retained far more of its original viscosity than the untreated taxiway's asphalt.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Flipkart, the Walmart-owned e-commerce major, is preparing to take on the long-standing food-delivery duopoly of Zomato and Swiggy.
articles.body: Flipkart, the Walmart-owned e-commerce major, is preparing to take on the long-standing food-delivery duopoly of Zomato and Swiggy. The move marks an entry into a highly contested sector that has previously seen tech titans such as Amazon and Google attempt to break in without success. The Bengaluru-headquartered platform is currently piloting the food-delivery service internally, expanding its team from a few hundred workers to more than 8,000 employees, a report has claimed.Citing people familiar with the matter, a report by TechCrunch claimed that to support the planned commercial rollout, Flipkart has assembled a dedicated fleet of delivery riders through its logistics division, Ekart. This delivery pool operates separately from the couriers managing its quick-commerce vertical.In-app integration and ‘Eat-in by Minutes’ brandingThe closed, employee-only service is integrated directly into Flipkart’s primary smartphone application, the report said, adding that it sits as an independent tab alongside the platform’s Minutes quick-commerce vertical and its travel booking portal. To power the catalog, Flipkart is tapping into two distinct restaurant pipelines:First is merchant listings accessed via the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), the government-backed open framework designed to link digital buyers and sellers across multiple platforms. And the second, local food outlets and dining establishments boarded directly by Flipkart.In Bengaluru, delivery personnel sporting uniforms with “Eat-in by Minutes” branding have already begun fulfilling trial meal orders across city streets, the report said.A fast-growing sector with room for new entrantsFlipkart is stepping into a food-delivery landscape that brokerage firm Bernstein estimates is expanding at 18% to 20% annually, the report said. Despite this growth, digital ordering still represents just over 15% of the total food-services market in India.The sector's leaders, Zomato (owned by Eternal) and Swiggy, currently cater to a combined base of 85 million to 95 million paying users each year, according to Bernstein data. While highlighting the firm grip held by the two companies, the metric underscores significant headroom for expansion in a country with over a billion internet subscriptions.Meanwhile, there are competitors that are experimenting with lower fees and budget-focused models:Rapido: The bike-taxi and ride-hailing company is scaling up Ownly, a food-ordering service operating on a zero-commission model for restaurants.Swiggy: The incumbent platform rolled out Toing, an independent application focused specifically on affordable, everyday meal options.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday said he would explain the opposition’s concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday said he would explain the opposition’s concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, delimitation and women’s reservation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 21.Speaking to reporters, Kharge said he had personally written to the Prime Minister and would raise all three issues with him.“I don't want to talk about politics today. I have personally written a letter to the Prime Minister, and he has two letters from me,” Kharge said.“I will explain everything to him tomorrow, including the harm caused by the SIR of electoral rolls, the implications of the delimitation exercise they are undertaking, and the issue of reservation for women. Why are they not implementing it? I will explain all these things tomorrow,” he added.On Monday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju responded to Kharge’s demand for an all-party meeting before Parliament takes up the proposed Delimitation Constitutional Amendment Bill. Rijiju said the government had repeatedly sought the Congress’s cooperation through written communications in March and April, as well as discussions with Kharge and Rahul Gandhi.He said the Congress had not provided dates for discussions despite repeated requests, prompting the government to consult other parties, including the DMK, Samajwadi Party, YSRCP, NCP, Shiv Sena (UBT), AIMIM and BJD.Rijiju also rejected allegations of procedural impropriety over the delay in proroguing Parliament after the Monsoon Session was adjourned sine die on August 13. He said there was no constitutional requirement prescribing a specific period for prorogation.The minister urged the Congress to cooperate constructively and refrain from obstructing important legislation.Earlier, Kharge had written to Modi, flagging what he called an “unprecedented” delay in proroguing the Monsoon Session and urging him to convene an all-party meeting to discuss any fresh delimitation proposals. He also cautioned against attempts to bulldoze a “far-reaching” Constitutional Amendment Bill through Parliament.In his letter, Kharge said 64 days had passed since the Monsoon Session was adjourned sine die on August 13, but neither House had been prorogued.Referring to the government's earlier legislative efforts, Kharge said the Bills had been made public late on April 14, followed by a special session on April 16. The Constitutional Amendment Bill on delimitation failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17.Kharge said he had written to Modi again on July 16 and August 27, reiterating the demand for an all-party meeting.“I am now doing so for a fourth time. Please convene an all-party meeting to have a detailed discussion on your new proposals before they are finalised for consideration in Parliament,” the Congress chief said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for a three-day visit to India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for a three-day visit to India.He is set to hold bilateral meeting with external affairs minister S Jaishankar focusing on strengthening ties between the two countries. The visit comes as Washington and New Delhi signal progress towards finalising a long-awaited trade agreement.Rubio is also scheduled to attend the “Freedom 250 Reception” at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai in the evening. On Wednesday, he will travel to Jamnagar in Gujarat, an important energy hub.US ambassador to India Sergio Gor and Rubio’s wife, Jeanette Dousdebes Rubio, were also present on his arrival.Ahead of their schedule, Rubio and Gor also visited the Gateway of India with Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis.Upon his arrival, Gor shared a picture of Rubio landing at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport with the caption, "Great to be back in Mumbai, this time with my friend Marco Rubio. Speaking to reporters in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Monday, Rubio said Washington was working to conclude the agreement.“We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. Rubio described India as an important ally and partner of the United States.He said Washington needed time to assess the economic implications of the proposed measures, including their potential impact on global energy supplies and prices.Ahead of Rubio’s visit, Jaishankar met a US Congressional delegation in Mumbai on Tuesday.
